name: CISplatin + Gemcitabine (NSCLC, squamous)
histology: squamous cell carcinoma (cisplatin/gemcitabine is preferred for squamous histology; gemcitabine is a preferred non-pemetrexed partner for squamous NSCLC)

biomarkers.note: Cytotoxic cisplatin/gemcitabine doublet, preferred for SQUAMOUS NSCLC (in a head-to-head RCT gemcitabine-containing therapy was more effective than pemetrexed in squamous histology; pemetrexed doublets are reserved for non-squamous). For NSCLC without an actionable oncogenic driver; driver-positive disease is directed to targeted therapy. Actionable drivers are much less common in squamous histology but molecular and PD-L1 testing are still recommended. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer, NSCL-E (Preferred squamous: Cisplatin/Gemcitabine).

lineOfTherapy: first-line for metastatic squamous NSCLC without an actionable driver; also a preferred neoadjuvant and adjuvant platinum doublet for squamous histology; not line-scoped in the perioperative setting

eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v7.2026, NSCL-E (Principles of Perioperative Systemic Therapy), Preferred (squamous): Cisplatin/Gemcitabine

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: no actionable oncogenic driver; driver-positive disease goes to targeted therapy
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v7.2026, Principles of Molecular and Biomarker Analysis

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function and performance status for cisplatin (nephrotoxic; requires hydration)
eligibilityCriteria.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 30, Non-small-cell Lung Cancer, ECOG 1505: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1 plus gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 (lines 68582 to 68585)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 68582 to 68585 (cisplatin 75 mg/m2 Day 1). ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Cisplatin requires vigorous IV hydration and monitoring for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neurotoxicity. NCCN NSCL-E lists Cisplatin/Gemcitabine as a preferred squamous doublet but does not print the per-cycle dose.

drugs.name: Gemcitabine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 30, Non-small-cell Lung Cancer, ECOG 1505: gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 (line 68584)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. line 68584 (gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8). Given every 21 days with cisplatin Day 1. Monitor for myelosuppression.

regimen.cycles: typically 4 cycles as a platinum doublet (metastatic first-line or perioperative); per clinical review

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: IV pre- and post-hydration with cisplatin to protect renal function.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: cisplatin is highly emetogenic; give high emetic-risk antiemetic prophylaxis.

supportiveCare: antiemetics: cisplatin-based regimen is high emetic risk; prophylaxis required on day of treatment
cisplatin hydration to reduce nephrotoxicity; monitor renal function, hearing, and peripheral neuropathy

monitoring: CBC before each dose (days 1 and 8) - gemcitabine myelosuppression
renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cycle - cisplatin nephrotoxicity
audiometry/hearing and peripheral neuropathy assessment - cisplatin ototoxicity and neurotoxicity

doseModificationRules.condition: low ANC or platelets on day 8
doseModificationRules.text: Day 8 gemcitabine is commonly reduced or omitted for day-8 cytopenias per protocol; clinical review required.
Cisplatin is nephrotoxic; consider carboplatin substitution or dose modification if renal function declines. Clinical review required.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 30, Non-small-cell Lung Cancer: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 Day 1 + gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8 (ECOG 1505, lines 68582 to 68585); gemcitabine more effective than pemetrexed in squamous histology (line 70770)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
guideline.locator: NSCL-E (Principles of Perioperative Systemic Therapy: Cisplatin/Gemcitabine listed as Preferred for squamous). NCCN prints the regimen name but not the per-cycle dose; dose is taken from the DeVita core layer.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for the cisplatin plus gemcitabine doublet in squamous NSCLC. Doses are grounded to the DeVita 12th ed. core layer: CISplatin 75 mg/m2 Day 1 plus Gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8 every 21 days (ECOG 1505, lines 68582 to 68585). Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v7.2026 NSCL-E list Cisplatin/Gemcitabine as a preferred squamous doublet and DeVita notes gemcitabine outperforms pemetrexed in squamous histology (line 70770), but NCCN does not print the per-cycle dose, so the numeric dose is sourced from DeVita rather than the guideline layer. This doublet is for NSCLC without an actionable oncogenic driver. ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin). Cisplatin hydration plus nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity/neurotoxicity monitoring and day-8 gemcitabine dose-modification for cytopenias are captured. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
